Peregrine to provide representative traffic trace and sample prompts by 2026-03-09

summary: High-level scoping for a 6-week POC to evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Peregrine's document summarization and routing use cases. Focus: success criteria (p95 latency, throughput, cost), workload sizing, bench plan, and timeline. Decided on side-by-side benchmarking of hosted and a dedicated reserved pool; private/on-prem deferred pending security gating for Q2. Action items and a 3-day benchmark plan were agreed.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~72 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Emma Liu (Peregrine Head of ML), Tom Becker (CTO), Jared Mills (Infra), Priya Anand (PM)

Summary: quick scoping for a POC comparing deployment modes and defining success criteria, workloads and benching plan.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on the account. Carlos from our SE team is here. Quick round robin?
[00:00:10] Emma Liu: Hi, Emma here. We'll be the ML team lead.
[00:00:13] Tom Becker: Tom, CTO. Good to meet you.
[00:00:16] Jared Mills: Jared, infra.
[00:00:18] Priya Anand: Priya, PM, focusing on SLOs and timelines.
[00:00:22] Carlos Rivera: Great, thanks. Agenda for today: capture success criteria, get rough workload numbers, agree a benchmark plan and landing timeline. We'll propose hosted vs dedicated bench configs and note what private would need.

[00:01:05] Emma Liu: Just to set context, our main workload is a document summarization + multi-step routing flow. Incoming PDFs -> extract -> summarize -> classify -> routing. About 200k requests per month right now. Bursty days where QPS spikes to ~65 for short windows. Average prompt tokens around 120, generation output 60 tokens.
[00:01:28] Maya Chen: helpful. Is that 200k unique requests or 200k API calls including downstream retries?
[00:01:32] Emma Liu: that's API calls, so it includes some retries. Net uniques closer to 160k.
[00:01:36] Jared Mills: Our infra requirement: data cannot leave the EU region for some customers, and for the highest-tier clients we need customer-managed keys (KMS). Right now we host in eu-west-1 for EU customers and us-west-2 for NA.
[00:01:52] Carlos Rivera: noted. For the POC, will you want to bench across region and roughly match your production traces?
[00:01:58] Tom Becker: yes, ideally. We want to see both regional latency and cross-region failover.

[00:02:30] Maya Chen: ok success criteria - can you read back what would make the POC a success for Peregrine?
[00:02:36] Priya Anand: From product: p95 end-to-end latency under 1.2s for the summarize step, p50 under 400ms for inference only. Cost: we want cost per 1M tokens processed to be below $X - TBD after you send pricing - but roughly 30% less than current cloud-hosted baseline. Reliability: <1% error on inference calls, 99.9% availability during business hours. Security: SOC2 compliance and KMS support.
[00:03:05] Emma Liu: Also model quality parity, we can't degrade summary ROUGE by more than 3 points compared to our current baseline model.
[00:03:12] Carlos Rivera: good. We'll include quality checks and prompt/payload parity. For latency numbers, we'll break out cold-start vs warm-path and tokenization overhead.

[00:03:50] Maya Chen: workload sizing — you gave 200k calls a month. Any plans for growth over the POC horizon?
[00:03:56] Emma Liu: expecting 30% growth over 3 months if POC proves. For POC bench planning we want a conservative 25% headroom, so plan for ~250k/month during bench.
[00:04:05] Jared Mills: concurrency: typical concurrency is 8-12 but during bursts we see 60+ concurrent streams hitting generation. We care about sustained QPS and tail latency.

[00:04:30] Speaker 1: (mumble) ok
[00:04:33] Carlos Rivera: For the dedicated config we'll propose a reserved pool sized to meet your p95 latency target at 1x and 2x concurrency (i.e., normal and burst). For hosted we'll show projected autoscale settings and expected cost delta.

[00:05:00] Tom Becker: question on private - we have a handful of customers that will require on-prem — is that realistic in Q2?
[00:05:06] Maya Chen: Private on-prem typically is a longer path. For Q2 you could do an initial VPC Private deployment with customer-managed KMS in our private offering, but fully air-gapped on-prem typically takes more procurement and an on-site ops window. We can scope that, but recommend POC first with hosted+dedi bench to validate perf and cost.
[00:05:30] Priya Anand: ok that matches our expectation.

[00:05:58] Emma Liu: Bench specifics — what are you proposing?
[00:06:02] Carlos Rivera: We're proposing a 3-day side-by-side bench: Day 1 baseline (your current infra), Day 2 Redwood Hosted with the same model and prompt set, Day 3 Redwood Dedicated reserved pool sized to your workload. We run identical traces and measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost, and quality checks. We'll also run a failover test and a KV cache warmup path.
[00:06:30] Maya Chen: We'll provide a bench config matrix with instance types, quantization settings, batch sizes, and tokenization flags.
[00:06:36] Emma Liu: for the dedicated env, will we get root-level access or logs? We need audit logs and token-level cost breakdowns.
[00:06:44] Carlos Rivera: You get per-request traces in the console, token-level cost estimations, and audit logs forwarded to your SIEM (we support S3/CloudTrail/ELK hooks). For dedicated we can enable deeper SSH-level access in a limited way for debugging, but production nodes are managed by Redwood.
[00:07:06] Jared Mills: encryption at rest and KMS?
[00:07:09] Maya Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS, HSM possible via enterprise add-on. Hosted supports tenant encryption and SOC2, and we can enable KMS for Private/VPC.
[00:07:20] Tom Becker: pricing - can you ballpark dedicated monthly commit vs hosted per-token for our workload?
[00:07:24] Maya Chen: ballpark only — we'll send a worksheet. Roughly, for workloads with stable throughput and high QPS, Dedicated often shows 20-40% lower per-token cost after commitments, whereas Hosted is higher per-token but no commit and faster time-to-value. Exact numbers in the worksheet.
[00:07:40] Priya Anand: important to model caching benefits too — we have repeated prefixes and a lot of shared context.
[00:07:45] Carlos Rivera: yes we'll include prefix cache hit rate scenarios; caching can dramatically reduce overall tokens generated and cost.
[00:07:52] Emma Liu: quality checks - how do you do regression detection?
[00:07:55] Carlos Rivera: we run a prompt set against each model/config and compute metrics you define (ROUGE, BLEU, custom heuristics), plus human review sample. We'll surface regressions in the console and tie alerts to rollout policies.
[00:08:12] Maya Chen: timeline proposal: 6-week POC
[00:08:15] Maya Chen: Week 0: kickoff and access/trace collection
[00:08:18] Maya Chen: Week 1: bench infra & config setup (dedicated pool provisioned)
[00:08:20] Maya Chen: Week 2: run baseline vs hosted bench
[00:08:23] Maya Chen: Week 3: dedicated bench and failover tests
[00:08:26] Maya Chen: Week 4: integration with your orchestration and metrics, cost tuning
[00:08:29] Maya Chen: Week 5: QA and security review for private option if needed
[00:08:32] Maya Chen: Week 6: decision and rollback plan
[00:08:35] Priya Anand: that timeline seems right, can you compress to 4 weeks if we reduce scope?
[00:08:40] Carlos Rivera: yes if we limit to core summarize flow and skip region cross testing we can compress to about 4 weeks. We'll note tradeoffs.
[00:08:46] Tom Becker: what about SLOs for cold starts? Some of our functions are invoked sporadically.
[00:08:50] Carlos Rivera: we measure cold start percentiles separately. For Dedicated we can keep warm pools to eliminate cold starts; Hosted has warm path guarantees but depends on load. We'll include a warmup strategy in the bench plan.
[00:09:10] Emma Liu: any risk of prompt leakage across tenants in hosted?
[00:09:14] Maya Chen: isolation is strong — we run customer isolation at the request routing layer, KV cache is tenant-scoped by default. We'll provide the security whitepaper.
[00:09:22] Jared Mills: audit and retention: we need 7 years of audit logs for a specific vertical client. Can Redwood meet that retention?
[00:09:28] Carlos Rivera: Yes for enterprise contracts we can provide extended log retention as an add-on and export to your S3 with encryption.
[00:09:35] Priya Anand: ok great.
[00:09:50] Speaker 2: (background noise)
[00:10:00] Maya Chen: Next, bench technical details - Carlos?
[00:10:03] Carlos Rivera: We'll run your trace through a replay harness, preserving inter-arrival times. For tokenization parity we'll ship a tokenizer container. Config matrix will include: model variant (float32 / int8 quantized), batch size, max tokens, kv cache enabled/disabled, concurrency levels. For dedicated we'll test two pool sizes (N and 2N) to simulate burst capacity. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 latency for generation-only and end-to-end. Also measure cost per 1M tokens and per-request.
[00:10:38] Emma Liu: will we be able to see raw logs for debugging?
[00:10:41] Carlos Rivera: yes, per-request logs are available, and we can stream them to your log collector. We'll obfuscate any PII by default but you can opt into raw for bench.
[00:10:51] Tom Becker: how do you handle model rollouts? If we pin a model and a newer variant comes, can we auto-fallback?
[00:10:56] Carlos Rivera: yes rollouts and canarying are built-in. You can pin model versions per-route and define fallbacks to lighter quantized variants when capacity constrained.
[00:11:08] Priya Anand: what about cost modeling around quantization?
[00:11:11] Carlos Rivera: quantized models give 2-3x throughput improvements with small quality delta for many workloads. We'll include quant perf/quality tradeoff table.
[00:11:20] Emma Liu: sample bench results would be great to see — any anonymized case studies?
[00:11:24] Maya Chen: we'll attach two anonymized case studies: one for a logistics customer and one for a fintech with strict KMS.
[00:11:30] Tom Becker: are there any known blockers for us running a dedicated pool in eu-west-1?
[00:11:34] Carlos Rivera: none on the Redwood side; we may need an SOC2 addendum if you need sustained KMS keys per customer. Provisioning a dedicated pool takes ~3-5 business days once the commit is done.
[00:11:50] Jared Mills: perf testing — do you support synthetic traffic shaping? We want to test tail scenarios.
[00:11:54] Carlos Rivera: yes we can simulate bursts, ramp tests, and repeated prefix scenarios for cache warming.
[00:12:05] Priya Anand: ok let's recap decisions and next steps
[00:12:08] Maya Chen: decisions: run a 3-day side-by-side bench (hosted vs dedicated). Private/on-preming deferred until security checklist passes. Success criteria: p95 < 1.2s summarize, p50 inference < 400ms, cost target TBD but aim for 20-40% improvement with dedicated after commit. Data residency: EU-only for EU customers. KMS available.
[00:12:28] Emma Liu: agreed.
[00:12:30] Tom Becker: agreed.
[00:12:33] Maya Chen: I'll send the benchmark plan and pricing worksheet by Friday (2026-03-06). Emma — you'll send traces and the prompt set by Monday (2026-03-09). Carlos will prepare the dedicated runbook and the cluster configs by 2026-03-13.
[00:12:50] Emma Liu: yes will do.
[00:12:52] Jared Mills: quick note: we'll need an internal security review before we go live with Private — flagging for the schedule.
[00:12:58] Maya Chen: noted, we'll coordinate with our security team once the bench is done.
[00:13:10] Priya Anand: can we get a short 30-min follow-up to review the bench plan next week?
[00:13:14] Maya Chen: absolutely, I'll propose times.
[00:13:20] Speaker 3: (laughter)
[00:13:30] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts.
[00:13:33] Meeting end.
